Improve the ability of the USG, host countries and other partners to prepare for and mitigate the effects of disasters, including both natural disasters and complex emergencies, taking into account the differences in men and womens freedom of movement and access to information. Activities under this component include any efforts to enhance the capacities of the USG (in Washington and in the field), humanitarian assistance providers, national host-country authorities, and local communities to engage in disaster reduction and response activities. Activities consist of standardized and coordinated assessments, monitoring, information sharing, data and situational analysis, joint planning; enhancement of coping mechanisms, including the capacity to address adaptation to constantly changing situations on the ground including climate variability and climate change.

title.narrative: HED Partnership: State University of Haiti/National Institute of Administration, Management and International Studies (INAGHEI) and the University of Massachusetts-Boston

description.narrative: The UMass Boston/INAGHEI University Partnership was a collaboration between the University of Massachusetts Boston (UMass Boston) and the State University of HaitiNational Institute of Administration, Management and International Studies (INAGHEI). The partnership focused on improving INAGHEIs Business Administration program to better meet demand in Haiti for trained business professionals and administrators. With the overall goal of improving INAGHEIs businessadministration program so that it can better prepare its students for business and the world of work.

Civil society has reached cross-roads in Haiti. After years of support for organizational capacity development, civic education and advocacy, new laws and policies are finally on the national agenda. This achievement will require Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) to shift toward more targeted advocacy, stronger public awareness campaigns, and to monitor the development, adoption and implementation of specific legislation. USAID will continue to support proactive civil society and community organizations, along with a more capable and independent media as they increasingly apply the skills they have learned through workshops, training, and direct technical assistance provided for the past ten years. These organizations will now be supported to play an even more active role in advocating for continued governance reform, monitoring policy implementation, and bridging the gap between citizens and their elected officials in order for Haitis burgeoning democracy to succeed.

The I-TRADE project tackles some of these underlying obstacles by addressing deficiencies and policy barriers in the public and private sectors. The project provides to the Government of Haiti (GOH) the tools necessary to effectively negotiate in the competitive global economy; build public sector institutional and ministerial capacity in investment and trade policy; and address weaknesses at the level of private sector institutions by strengthening their ability to be proactive and reactive.

Establish and/or develop a broadly functioning independent media sector, which is a crucial factor in democratic governance. Building this sector is accomplished through such activities as providing infrastructure and equipment to ensure access to information, shaping the media legal and regulatory environment, boosting professional capacity of the media sector, promoting sustainability through encouraging media-related business development and sound financial/management practices, and supporting advocacy and networking among media sector organizations.

description.narrative: Improve the capacity and sustainability of civil and criminal justice sector actors and institutions, enhance coordination amongst them, develop citizen demand for an effective and accountable justice system, and develop associations to advocate for all citizens. Justice sector actors and institutions include: police, border security, prosecutors, forensics experts, judges, court personnel, public defenders, corrections personnel, private bar, law schools, legal professional associations, and training institutions for each of them. Work towards an equitable justice system by ensuring equality before the law, fair trial standards, and other elements of procedural fairness. Ensure more equitable access to justice through innovations within and beyond the state system and through improvements in the quality and quantity of justice services, with a particular focus on women, youth, the poor, and other marginalized or vulnerable groups. Improve the capacity and sustainability of civil and criminal justice sector actors and institutions, enhance coordination amongst them, develop citizen demand for an effective and accountable justice system, and develop associations to advocate for all citizens. Justice sector actors and institutions include: police, border security, prosecutors, forensics experts, judges, court personnel, public defenders, corrections personnel, private bar, law schools, legal professional associations, and training institutions for each of them. Work towards an equitable justice system by ensuring equality before the law, fair trial standards, and other elements of procedural fairness. Ensure more equitable access to justice through innovations within and beyond the state system and through improvements in the quality and quantity of justice services, with a particular focus on women, youth, the poor, and other marginalized or vulnerable groups. Programs primarily focused on trafficking in persons or migrant smuggling should be included in element 5.3 under the Transnational Crime area in the Peace and Security Objective.

title.narrative: LOKAL (Limye ak Oganizasyon pou Kolektivite yo Ale Lwen)

description.narrative: The LOKAL (Limy ak ganizasyon pou Kolektivite yo Ale Lwen) project was designed after the return of democracy with the election of Preval in 2006. The project focused on three primary areas of intervention: improving decentralization policy and the legal framework, increasing the capacity of local governments to effectively govern and provide basic public services, and enhancing transparent local governance through citizen participation and public information. In addition, LOKAL established several models for communal participatory planning, and piloted a system for increasing municipal tax revenues in three communes. Project implementation was interrupted several times due to natural disasters, most notably from the 2008 hurricane season and the 2010 earthquake, and the project was modified in both cases to respond to emerging needs.

The power sector utility, Electricit dHaiti (EDH), faces considerable technical, commercial, and managerial challenges. Under the Transition Management Contract (TMC), a private third party will temporarily manage EDH operations in selected areas to improve financial and technical operations. TMC is a first step in a GOH plan to rehabilitate the sector so as to expand service, increase access, and improve reliability and commercial performance. The goal for the restructuring of the electricity sector as part of the Haiti Energy Access and Reform Initiative is to build an efficient and financially sound sector that operates within a competitive and transparent market, attracts capital, and is able to reliably and affordably satisfy current and forecasted demands for electricity services. In order to achieve these objectives, we awarded a contract to Tetra Tech, an experienced utility manager, to implement TMCa key element in support of this goal.

Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

description.narrative: Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

(Haiti): .In its final year of implementation, Project Sante will focus on delivering the main components of the Ministry of Health (MOH) Essential Package of Services (ESP) to reduce morbidity, mortality, and the burden of disease for 4.5 million Haitians. As described in the approved Country Operational Plan (COP) 21, HIV activities will be implemented in community settings through the community health worker (CHW) network to facilitate self-testing, drug distribution, adherence classes and support groups, and samples collection for viral load testing...Maternal health interventions will train health care providers to consistently use referral and counter-referral forms. Working through Mothers' Clubs, these interventions will be used to promote MOH antenatal care recommendations such as encouraging pregnant women to enroll early into the Mothers' Clubs, complete four antenatal visits, and to deliver at a health facility attended by trained health providers. To deliver vaccination and nutrition services to children, Project Sante, together with community members, will use targeted strategies including catch-up vaccination campaigns, which allow a steady coverage from one trimester to the next. To address the reported rise in malnutrition, Project Sante will continue screenings, referrals for treatment, and follow-up at the community level...Projet Sante will also continue to support the provision of modern family planning options and in collaboration with the MOH, will provide integrated supervision and site management to continuously improve facilities' abilities to provide quality services. ..Water and sanitation technical leads will train and retrain site personnel on infection control and prevention and re-activate chlorine distribution for routine disinfection as part of the COVID-19 response...

description.narrative: (Haiti): Through the Small Grants Facility (SGF), USAID/Haiti makes small grants available to local organizations to build sustainable local capacity to achieve key development objectives. As Haiti is especially vulnerable to shocks and stresses both from natural disasters and socio-economic instability, FY 2018 funds will support resilience activities to introduce complementary agricultural programming into target communities. The primary objective will be to link communities receiving direct food assistance to opportunities to increase agricultural income and improve resilience. This activity supports USAID/Haiti's Strategic Framework Development Objective 2 (DO2), Intermediate Result 2.1, "vulnerable households better able to weather shocks and chronic stresses," and will be carried out jointly by the Food for Peace, Economic Growth and Agriculture, and Health offices. The small grants utilizing FY18 funding will target: 1) agricultural productivity; 2) support to agribusinesses including livestock production and small and medium size commercial farms; 3) implementation of nutrition sensitive agriculture; and 4) capacity building of community based organizations to implement disaster risk reduction activities...

title.narrative: Public International Organization grant for Build Back Safer Activity in Haiti

description.narrative: Public International Organization grant for Build Back Safer Activity in Haiti

(Haiti): The Community-Driven Development (CDD) activity encourages community engagement in municipal-level governance, an important contribution to USAID/Haiti's development objective of improving the accountability and independence of governance institutions in Haiti. Building upon previous USAID support to local governments and their success in fostering collaboration between citizens and municipal officials, the CDD activity supports the local population and municipal officials to identify and address their needs by developing a public list of priority projects and a longer-term strategic development plan. The water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) sector is of particular importance under this activity, as it has been one of the most frequently requested areas for intervention by local populations. CDD will increase citizen participation in local government planning and decision making; support improved access to clean water and sanitation; support improved public service delivery; and increase access to education. The program will also focus on hiring local residents to work on the interventions to bolster community buy-in as well as to create short-term employment for the communities. By engaging local community residents, particularly youth, in the identification of priority needs and in the implementation of small-scale development projects, this activity improves ownership of and engagement with local governance and develops the capacity of communities to solve their own local problems... .. .. .

title.narrative: Project Supporting the Efficient Management of State Resources - GERE

description.narrative: (Haiti): With FY 2021 funds, the Project Supporting the Efficient Management of State Resources (GERE) aims to contribute to the decentralization efforts of the GOH by addressing long-standing issues that impede better governance in Haiti. The project will advance the Mission's objective to improve independent and accountable GOH institutions. With an all-Haitian staff and a consortium of two local institutions-the Institute for Training and Services (IFOS) and the Center for Training and Technical Coaching (CFET)-RTI International is well-placed for this governance initiative. The Project will support select municipal, departmental, and central level GOH entities' ability to integrate best governance practices to improve domestic resource mobilization and planning to combat corruption for the improvement of public service delivery. Building on USAID activities, GERE will leverage past, current, and upcoming development efforts to facilitate demand-driven, locally owned, and effective coordination and collaboration in development programming, including contributing to the findings of the Organization for Economic Development and Coordination's public governance review. GERE will also support key GOH institutions to build leadership and advocacy skills at the national and local levels and support them to better understand their roles and responsibilities, strengthen their governance processes and mechanisms while increasing civic engagement. Given the volatility of the Haitian governance landscape, the project will continue to use adaptive management approaches to reach its objectives. ......

description.narrative: (Haiti): .The Health Leadership Project (HLP) is a five-year activity supporting USAID's Vision for Health Systems Strengthening. USAID will support the Ministry of Health (MOH) to better plan and manage three essential functions: 1) governance; 2) financing; and 3) human resources. HLP is USAID's key activity to support the Government of Haiti (GOH) in developing concrete and actionable domestic resource mobilization for health strategies in Haiti. .HLP activities are both MCH and PEPFAR funded. For the remaining period of the agreement (Oct 2021-April 2024), HLP will use FY2021 funds to continue to provide oversight and technical support to the GOH as the governance, financing, and human resources for health activities currently under HLP transition to local partners, Centre de Formation et d'Encadrement Technique (CFET) and Groupe Croissance (GC). During this time, Management Sciences for Health (MSH) will continue to work closely with the HLP local solutions partners (as part of new awards HLP/Health Finance and HLP/Human Resources for Health), to ensure their capacity is strengthened to provide technical support activities with the MOH to lead and finance the health sector and improve its planning and oversight of the health workforce. ..Transitioning into an oversight role for the remaining period, MSH will coach the partners to strengthen their relationship with the MOH and their technical leadership on HLP activities by providing high-quality technical support to the MOH in Health Finance (HF) and Human Resources for Health (HRH)..

title.narrative: Strong Beginnings: Leveraging the Home, School and Church to Develop the Whole Child in Haiti (New GDA)

description.narrative: (Haiti): With FY 2021 funds, USAID will support the new activity Strong Beginnings: Leveraging the Home, School and Church to Develop the Whole Child in Haiti to improve reading and writing outcomes in Creole and French in approximately 160 schools in the Grand'Anse and South departments. The activity aligns with USAID's Education Policy and supports the Mission's resilience focus objectives..Activities will undertake teacher training and coaching efforts, including training in the use of classroom libraries to enhance students' reading comprehension, remediation/differentiation of instruction, and use of a bilingual, scripted, phonics-based early grade literacy curriculum embedded in a social-emotional learning approach. Pre-primary education will also be included to focus on the essential pre-literacy skills and to create an enabling learning environment from the beginning of a child's education through the early grades. The implementation of a learning laboratory approach facilitates a rapid feedback model that builds systematic achievement of learning objectives into the early stages of pre-primary education..Expected results include improved writing and reading skills in Creole and French for first and second grade students; improved social and emotional learning (SEL) skills for teachers and students; improved school readiness measures; implementation of a robust monitoring and evaluation plan; increased access to quality teacher training and coaching; knowledge sharing events among stakeholders in Haiti; the establishment of networks to develop partnerships in education across five departments in Haiti...

title.narrative: Haiti Resilience and Agriculture Sector Advancement (HRASA)

description.narrative: (Haiti): ..The Haiti Resilience and Agriculture Sector Advancement (HRASA) activity's goal is to increase individual, household, and community resilience by establishing sustainable and inclusive agricultural market systems that are resistant to shocks and stresses. The activity will be implemented in Resilience Focus Zones (RFZs) located in the north and northeast, the Central Plateau, and the south. ..HRASA will advance three integrated objectives: increasing market system efficiency; incentivizing private sector investment and engagement; and improving the ability of households and communities to recover from shocks and stresses. HRASA will employ a facilitative market systems approach to expand opportunities in order to build competitive, inclusive, and resilient agricultural market systems. While building off of value chain (VC) opportunities, this market systems approach looks at the wider context in which households and communities interact with multiple, interconnected VCs and catalyzes actions to change behaviors that impede agricultural market efficiency, private sector engagement, and participation of poor and marginalized groups. .With FY2022 funds, these interventions will likely include support for research and extension services to increase farm productivity for selected agricultural commodities; the creation of public-private-partnerships involving private firms and farmers to create sustainable market systems; and the implementation of a strategy that builds farmers' resilience. To support the Mission's resilience-building programs in the RFZs, Feed the Future, and Offices of Humanitarian Assistance and Education activities will seek to integrate across sectors to leverage impacts in economic growth, agricultural development, education, health, water and sanitation, governance, and nutrition.. .

description.narrative: Since the end of August 2021, there are thousands of Haitians assembling in makeshift sites on the Mexican side of the border to wait while deciding whether to attempt entry into the U.S. carrying their belongings, the migrants have been traversing the ankle-deep river between Mexico and Texas. As of 17 September, there were about 13,700 new arrivals in Del Rio City. While repatriations of Haitian migrants from the U.S. to Haiti had been paused after the devastating earthquake on 14 August, this sudden surge in migrant crossings over the past weeks has prompted it to change course. The International Organization of Migration (IOM) aims to support the improvement of reception facilities to better welcome migrants upon their return to Haiti, both in Port-Au-Prince and Cap-Haitian. This will enable key stakeholders involved in migrant assistance to be prepared for repatriations and stand ready to welcome migrants even when informed in a very short notice.

(Haiti): In the agriculture sector, innovation and evidence-based approaches that are adapted to local conditions are critical to increasing production and productivity, transforming goods, and creating and strengthening market linkages. Growing the base of specific skill sets helps address complex issues such as building human and institutional capacity and identifying areas of research for the benefit of local institutions and producers. The Agricultural University Partnership activity aims to support a network of Haitian institutions in developing an agricultural research agenda that is aligned with national development, food security, and resilience priorities. The goal is to create a center that will strengthen agricultural education, training, research, and outreach activities, and link farmers with the private sector. Using FY 2022 funding, this activity will increase institutional capacities and social capital to better meet the needs of the agricultural sector in Haiti, develop revenue-generating services at local institutions to ensure that farmers have continued access to services, and support research centers to showcase high-potential agricultural technologies and strategies to sustainably intensify smallholder production systems..The focus on local institutions aligns with the mission's integrated resilience-focused strategy and aims to have deeper engagements with local universities and research centers in Haiti, more specifically in the two mission-designated Resilience Focus Zones. Given the continued interest in agriculture professions and the capacity to conduct applied research, USAID plans to use FY 2022 funds to better connect academic institutions to the private sector, extension organizations, and farmers. This activity will contribute to addressing the challenges associated with variable cropping systems, low productivity, and support demand-driven applied research.... .

title.narrative: HLP/ Human Resources for Health (HRH) Activity Award

description.narrative: (Haiti): The Health Leadership Project / Human Resources for Health (HLP/HRH) award will support the Government of Haiti's (GOH) Ministry of Health (MOH) to improve planning and management related to two essential functions: 1) Governance; and 2) Human Resources for Health (HRH). This award is USAID's primary investment toward ensuring the Government of Haiti (GOH) continues the implementation of the HRH strategy and implements the HRH transition plan of USG-supported workers to the GOH budget. . .Using FY 2022 funds, specific interventions include:.Support to the MOH Department of Human Resources with the implementation of the National Human Resources Plan..Support to the MOH in the consolidation and implementation of the Special Statute of the Public Service for Health in collaboration with the Office De Management et Des Ressources Humaines and other actors in the health sector.Support the MOH to strengthen human resource management.Support the review of the transition plan in collaboration with all stakeholders including Global Fund..Assist the MOH in the establishment and implementation of the Operational Workforce Planning Unit..Improve the availability of government-controlled health human resources for sustainable HIV services through a viable transition plan.. .The Centre de Formation et d'Encadrement Technique, the implementing partner of this award, has collaborated with Management Science for Health throughout the first two years of the activity to acquire the technical skills and managerial capacities enabling them becoming direct recipients of the transition award from USAID in April 2022. The award supports the USG's goal to build local capacity and sustainability of its investments in Haiti. .

description.narrative: (Haiti): .The Health Leadership Program / Health Financing (HLP/HF) award will continue to support Haiti's Ministry of Health (MOH) to improve planning and management related to two essential functions: 1) Governance and 2) Health Financing. The activity represents USAID's primary investment toward ensuring the Government of Haiti develops and implements domestic resource mobilization strategies, including advocacy for greater investment in health. Although the HLP/HF activity will be implemented by Group Croissance (GC), the implementer will closely collaborate with its counterpart in coordination with Management Sciences for Health (MSH) and Centre de Formation et d'Encadrement Technique (CFET). GC's initial step will focus on engaging MOH leadership and ensuring that the proposed activities address the priorities and needs for health financing. Using FY 2022 funds, specific interventions include:-Support to MOH's Studies and Programming Unit to develop a health financing strategy. To ensure successful implementation, the award will strengthen the relationship between the MOH and other key ministries, specifically the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Planning-Provision of technical assistance to the MOH to continue to study the health insurance context in Haiti, including the level of population coverage.-Study of catastrophic health expenditures on household and social inequities in health.-Support to MOH to improve the public financial management at institutional and departmental levels.GC has collaborated with MSH throughout the first two years of the activity to acquire the technical skills and managerial capacities enabling them to become direct recipients of the transition award from USAID in April 2022. Continued success of the award's activities directly contribute to a more robust and reliable health system in Haiti that decreases illegal migration in search of better health systems which is a top US priority.

title.narrative: IHSD- Partnerships for Equity in Health

description.narrative: (Haiti): The Improved Health Service Delivery (IHSD) - Partnerships for Equity in Health Activity (PEH), will build on and expand on USAID's efforts to address key drivers of maternal and child health. These include morbidity and mortality, family planning/reproductive health, water, sanitation and hygiene, nutrition, HIV/AIDS, and health system strengthening. This five-year activity will increase access to integrated health care with a strong emphasis on quality and patient-centered primary health services to ensure a continuum of care and efficient use of resources including technologies, best practices, and innovation to support sustainable health service delivery. .With FY 2022 funds IHSD-PEH will provide health services in four geographical departments in 30 facilities and surrounding communities. The proposed activities will: ..promote inclusive approaches and increased local ownership; .identify and mobilize domestic resources; .strive to empower communities; and adopt innovative strategies that lead to the provision of quality and affordable health services for all-around improved health outcomes, and ultimately, a resilient health system. ..This activity will be implemented by a locally established partner and will leverage the bi-directional referral system with processes for tracking and feedback to enable the strongest possible linkage between community-based and facility-based care. The activity will work to fully empower community health workers to improve health within communities via counseling and positive behavior modeling during home visits, at rally points and community meetings and other local activities. Community health workers will also receive support to strengthen their ability to gather patient well-being and monitoring data...

description.narrative: (Haiti): The Integrated Health Resilience Activity (IHRA) will implement evidence-based approaches to improve health outcomes in maternal/newborn/child health (MNCH), family planning/reproductive health, nutrition, HIV, and issues related to COVID-19. IHRA will strengthen Haiti's health systems by supporting progress on GOH's health priorities while promoting equity, quality, and resource optimization. It will also provide primary health care services to Haitians in 139 facilities and surrounding communities in six departments (Nord, Nord-Est, Nord-Ouest, Artibonite, Centre, and Ouest). Using FY 2022 funds, interventions will:-Build the capacity of health care providers to consistently provide antenatal, delivery, and postnatal services-Promote antenatal care recommendations through referral and counter-referral mechanisms to and through Mothers' Clubs-Deliver and expand acute malnutrition services plus routine and COVID-19 vaccinations in healthcare facilities by using "Reaching Every Community" strategies including Rally Post and community-based events-Continue to support the provision of modern family planning methods-In collaboration with the MOH provide integrated supervision and site management that improves facilities' abilities to provide quality services.-Implement water, sanitation, and hygiene strategies in facilities' interventions and-Train site personnel on infection control and prevention, waste management, and chlorine distribution for routine disinfection as part of the COVID-19 response.IHRA's expected results include: 1) Maternal, newborn, child health, nutrition and family planning/reproductive health outcomes improved through provision of quality service delivery; 2) comprehensive HIV services provided in order to achieve epidemic control in Haiti; and 3) improved health systems through the promotion of quality of care, empowerment of communities, data for results and resource optimization. ..

title.narrative: Financing Climate Resilient Sanitation Systems and Services (SANIFIN)

description.narrative: Under this activity, USAID will provide technical assistance to utilities, service providers, and local authorities in Haiti to enable them to access traditional and non-traditional financing, enhance domestic budget allocations through increased revenue collection in order to upgrade and expand climate-resilient sanitation systems and services. USAID SANIFIN will pursue the following objectives: 1) strengthen management and financial viability of sanitation services providers to be ready to access capital; 2) facilitate partnership opportunities and models that increase the availability of affordable, climate-resilient sanitation systems and sustainable sanitation services; and 3) increase capacity of finance providers to serve the sanitation sector. The activity takes a systems approach to improve resilience of the Haitian sanitation sector, integrating resilience into the implementation of capacity building and social behavior change, and demonstrates how local systems and services strengthening and sector resilience are mutually reinforcing.

description.narrative: The purpose of the Haiti Livestock Innovation Activity entitled Systme dInnovation en Production Animale (SIPA) is to increase the long-term productivity and resilience of the livestock sector in Haiti, particularly two resilience focus zones (RFZ). One RFZ in the Southern Region and the other in the North-North-East-Central Plateau Region. The activity will take into consideration the unique production environments, priority animals, potential for improvement, and existing resources. SIPA aims to improve the productivity of livestock in the RFZs by seeking localized solutions for animal nutrition and developing a long-term strategy to improve the genetic stock of priority animals such as goats and cattle. Also, this activity will work in conjunction with the livestock market systems (LMS) activity to inform and complement its work as it is also focused on increasing the productivity and sales of key livestock from a market systems approach. There will be opportunities to apply and disseminate findings from this research activity through the LMS to individuals and businesses. In addition, this activity will also partner with local partner universities in coordination with the Haiti University Partnerships (HUP) Activity. HUP will build the institutional capacity of local agriculture universities and this activity will partner with them to conduct research, disseminate findings, and potentially establish revenue generating activities in the sector. The project goals will be achieved through the following research objectives: improve the genetic profile of key livestock species (small ruminants, dairy and beef cattle) through breeding and dissemination of quality genetic stock in Haiti. Increase the performance of livestock through transformative forage and feed interventions. Build the academic, vocational and research capacity of key local universities and support dissemination of these new research findings.

The key sub-watersheds will be determined later during the co-creation process. This goal is supported by two primary intertwined objectives: 1. Rehabilitate critical sub watersheds; and 2. Strengthen community-led natural resources.

title.narrative: Justice Renewal and Advancement Program (JRAP) Activity

description.narrative: The overall goal of JRAP is improve the efficiency, transparency, and accountability of the justice system in the short- to- mid-term while expanding the availability of legal services and the ability to adjudicate cases fairly (safeguarding citizens rights) and efficiently, all in a sustainable fashion that instills increased public confidence in the justice system. JRAP comprises two main programming components that are further outlined below. In alignment with USAIDs new Rule of Law policy, JRAP is designed with a People-Centered Justice (PCJ) approach that improves the user experiences of justice systems on both sides of the system by ensuring that USAIDs assistance and the justice services (formal and informal) are evidence-based, data-driven, user-friendly, solution-focused, prevention-oriented, and pathway-multiplying that they expand access to justice services. Using people-centered approaches, JRAP will work with both sides of the justice system to impact how justice processes address Haitis critical problem with pre-trial detention, as well as, to the extent possible, issues of corruption in the justice system.

In Haiti, CHF International is undertaking the KATA program. KATA, which stands for the Creole Konbit Ak Tet Ansanm, the principle of working together to accomplish a common goal, is a program designed to create long and short term employment for the people of Haiti, a country with an unemployment rate estimated at around 60%. CHF International does this through community involvement in rehabilitation of infrastructure projects and through helping existing industries to increase their capacity, efficiency and reach new markets. After the disastrous tropical storm season of 2008, CHF is also partnering with the community in order to reduce the risks of flooding, destruction and loss of life caused by hurricanes and other adverse weather.

title.narrative: Community Health and AIDS Mitigation Project (CHAMP)

description.narrative: USAID partner FHI 360 is leading a team of non-governmental organizations (NGOs) to implement CHAMP. The project is structured around the development of community-based service delivery points (CSDPs), which provide reproductive health/family planning, maternal and child health services, tuberculosis management, and nutrition and social assistance to communities. CHAMP primarily targets people living with HIV/AIDS (PLHA), orphans and vulnerable children (OVC), and their families. Referrals and home visits are key components of this community-based program.

title.narrative: Haiti Integrated Financing for Value Chains and Enterprises (HIFIVE)

description.narrative: HIFIVE is a suppport to the financial sector initiative. HIFIVEs principal goal is to increase access to finance for households and micro, small and medium-sized enterprises that are located primarily in semi-urban, rural and agricultural areas.One of HIFIVE key tool to achieve its goal of financial inclusion is the promotion and the support for the increased use of Information Communication Technology,with a focus on Mobile Money, to help expand the institutions reach while reducing the cost of the services over time.

Objectives for Haiti: HIFIVE aims to: (1) Support rural and agricultural value chain access to credit and other financial products and services, and (2) Support the use of ICT primarily mobile money, to promote financial inclusion.

title.narrative: Leadership, Management & Sustainability Project In Haiti

description.narrative: The award will address four objectives: (1) strengthen local capacity to manage the supply chain of USAID-donated condoms and family planning (FP) commodities; (2) strengthen the capacity of the Ministry of Public Health and Population (MSPP) FP Program to manage commodity logistics and provide quality FP services at major public sector hospitals; (3) strengthen the capacity and leadership of the MSPP to plan, supervise, and coordinate community mobilization activities for HIV/AIDS and other programs, with particular focus on the regional health department level; and (4) implement leadership training and capacity building tools of the LMS Project to strengthen local NGO and public sector partners.

title.narrative: Prevention of Sexual Transmission of HIV/AIDs in Haiti

description.narrative: PrevSIDA aims to increase understanding of patterns and settings of risky sexual behavior; increase risk assessment, condom use, and condom availability; and increase access to HIV, health, and other services.

Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. (Haiti): The Haiti Nutrition Security Program (NSP) strategy, implemented by Partners of the Americas, is based on a holistic community health, nutrition, and livelihood approach. With FY 2015 resources, the project will continue to recruit and provide support to Mother Leaders, and organize them into Care Groups. Each Mother Leader is then responsible for directing and chairing local neighborhood women's clubs, through which nutrition counseling and best health practices will be shared with additional young pregnant and lactating mothers (of children under the age of five). As a result, the NSP is now reaching over 15,446 neighborhood households, and is expected to reach 21,000 households over the life of the project.

title.narrative: Aksyon Kominotè nan Sante pou Ogmente Nitrisyon (AKSYON) Nutrition Program

description.narrative: (Haiti): "Aksyon Kominote nan Sante pou Ogmante Nitrisyon" (AKSYON), a five-year health and nutrition activity, addresses the core issues that contribute to malnutrition in Haiti. The project directly supports the Government of Haiti's efforts to manage maternal and child health and nutrition-related diseases, including tracking malnutrition among women and children at the community level and referral for treatment. With FY 2020 funds, AKSYON will expand nutrition interventions in all ten departments, including in the drought-affected areas in the northern part of the country (North West, North, and North East), and will improve knowledge and skills-building around essential components of child and adult nutrition. The program outcomes include: reducing the number of stunted children; ensuring programs are data-driven; improving the cost-effectiveness of nutrition programs; scaling up community management of acute malnutrition; increasing positive behavior changes in water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) practices; and improving nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive WASH knowledge, skills, and practices. In specific cases when the malnourished children live in hard to reach areas and the referral to a close health center is not feasible, AKSYON will provide Ready to Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) to the children for treatment and do the follow up. AKSYON interventions aim at mass screening of children under five and pregnant women for malnutrition. In collaboration with the Sante Project, AKSYON refers acute malnourished children to facilities for health care, treatment, and also HIV testing under PEPFAR-funded activities... .. .. .

(Haiti): USAID/Haiti's food fortification project (RANFOSE), co-funded by HIV funding, continues to improve health and nutrition outcomes by addressing micronutrient deficiencies and food fortification. Micronutrient deficiencies are a major challenge in Haiti. Based on the 2016-2017 Demographic Health Survey data, 66 percent of children under five are anemic, as are 49 percent of women of reproductive age. The RANFOSE project works with importers, distributors, and local food producers to fortify wheat flour with iron and folic acid, vegetable oil with vitamin A, and salt with iodine. Through the support of this activity, Vitamin A fortified oil was introduced for the first time in the Haitian market...FY 2022 resources will continue to be used to:..Increase the availability of high-quality, fortified staple foods across the country by expanding local production and increasing imports of fortified foods, .Provide clear, consistent, and useful messaging for wholesale and retail consumers on the value and safety of fortified foods. .Continue and extend media campaigns that encourage the use of fortified foods, including cooking oil fortified with Vitamin A, iodized salt, and fortified wheat flour..Continue to support the National Food Quality Laboratory, which provides testing to assure that micronutrients are present at the stated levels in fortified foods. ..The project will continue to strengthen the capacity of the Government of Haiti to address critical issues related to sustained and effective food fortification programs. RANFOSE directly supports and contributes to the government-led efforts to improve the nutrition, health, and food security of the Haitian population..

(Haiti): .The USAID Reforestation Project aims to address environmental degradation and loss of tree cover in the north and northeast regions of Haiti by supporting community resilience and providing environmental services. The activity pursues four primary objectives: 1) Reduce the threat of deforestation, including threats to mangrove forests; 2) Improve community resilience to economic and natural shocks and stresses; 3) Increase tree cover in targeted watersheds; and 4) Improve environmental governance and coordination. With FY 2021 funds, the activity will consolidate the achievements of previous years and develop exit strategies to ensure the sustainability of those interventions. The activity will continue with landscape restoration interventions through the production and planting of more than one million fruit and forest trees, including mangroves. The activity will also develop value chain development strategies to link smallholder farmers who work on productive agroforestry systems to markets. In addition, technical assistance will be provided with the aim to convert the energy usage of 15,000 food street vendors to Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG). This will reduce the demand for charcoal and wood and therefore mitigate the threat of deforestation. ..This activity is designed to expand community-level success to a larger scale of impact by empowering local stakeholders to develop plans for landscape and watershed restoration. By employing an integrated and holistic approach, the USAID Reforestation Project is the best intervention to help the communities meet their livelihood and energy needs while simultaneously supporting existing and developing forested areas. .All EG.11.3 $445,052 meets the Sustainable Landscapes and Haiti Reforestation directive..All EG.13.2 $3,375,000 contributes to the Adaptations and Haiti Reforestation directive......

title.narrative: Tout Timoun Ap Li - ToTAL (All Children Reading)

description.narrative: ToTAL, a 29-month USAID-funded applied research project, was launched in August 2012 and simultaneously addressed two pressing concerns for Haiti: education and literacy. Early grade reading is not only a priority for the Ministre de lEducation Nationale et de la Formation Professionnelle (Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training [MENFP]) but also the primary focus of USAID basic education efforts worldwide. Many donors, including the World Bank and the United Nations Childrens Fund (UNICEF), operate in Haiti and support the government efforts, and they are collaborating with the Government of Haiti (GOH) to promote access to and quality of education. The USAID mission in Haiti is leading this effort to work with and reinforce the capacity of the MENFP to promote early grade reading for the majority of Haitian children.

description.narrative: MSH's Sant pour le Dveloppement et la Stabilit dHati (SDSH II) projectknown as Pwoj Djanm (robust project) in Creoleand its all-Haitian team are working to increase availability of essential social services, reduce internal conflict, enable productive livelihoods that contribute to Haitis economic development, and build capacity as the foundation for progress.

The three-year KONEKTE (KONesans E Konpetans TEknik) program is designed to alleviate capacity constraints in Haitian Ministries by identifying and placing experienced Technical Advisors in critical posts to support the implementation of the Government of Haitis Action Plan for National Recovery and Development of Haiti and the United States Governments Post-Earthquake Strategy in Haiti. KONEKTE works closely with the OMRH to identify high level advisors through a transparent and competitive recruitment process that prioritizes the skills and expertise of Haitian Nationals and Diaspora. Each advisor is placed in a Ministry in order to fill an existing skills gap. Specific assignments vary in content and duration as needs are identified in collaboration with each Ministry.

title.narrative: Limye ak Oganizasyon pou Kolektivite yo Ale Lwen Plus (LOKAL+)

description.narrative: (Haiti): USAID's local governance project, Limyak Oganizyon pou Kolektivite yo ale Lwen Plus (LOKAL+), implements activities in eight to ten communes in an effort to increase local government capacity through targeted technical assistance for participatory planning, budgeting, tax collection, and managing municipal resources. LOKAL+ aims to improve public services in targeted communes located within the three USG development corridors by achieving the following expected results: 1) strengthened communal government capacity to provide services; 2) increased local revenues to pay for local services; 3) greater access to public funding and services for communal governments, including improved access to Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH); 4) improved national-level policy and legislation in support of local services; and 5) increased transparency, oversight and accountability of local governments and their service providers. FY2015 funds specifically will contribute to improved access to WASH in targeted municipalities by funding high-priority WASH projects identified by select communal governments

description.narrative: (Haiti): The Health Information Systems (HIS) project will support USG efforts to strengthen the Ministry of Health's (MOH) capacity to build sustainable health information systems within Haiti, allowing for the GOH to effectively manage program resources (both host country and donor) and monitor patient outcomes, as well as to ensure effective, routinized information use throughout the health sector. In early FY 2014, HIS helped the MOH define gaps and adopt a health information system (DHiS2), linking the various information systems currently in use, and by the end of that year, the project created a national data warehouse to facilitate data analysis and informed resource and management planning. With FY 2016 resources, HIS will provide focused capacity building to the MOH's Unit of Evaluation and Planning (UEP) to allow the unit to develop and enforce MOH strategic information regulations and standards related to monitoring and reporting of Haiti's health activities.

title.narrative: Feed the Future-North : Appui à la Valorisation du potentiel Agricole du Nord, à la Sécurité Economique et Environnementale (AVANSE)

description.narrative: (Haiti): Agriculture is central to the Haitian economy, generating nearly 25 percent of GDP and employing more than 60 percent of the population. Agriculture is especially important in Haiti's predominantly rural northern corridor. The Feed the Future North (FTFN) project supports the objective of increasing the incomes of at least 28,000 rural households through: 1) increased agricultural productivity; 2) stabilized hillsides above selected plains; and 3) strengthened agricultural markets. Rice, plantain/banana and cacao are the value chains supported by FTFN. In FY 2018, FTFN will increase the productivity of these value chains by providing access to improved technologies, management practices, and irrigation water. The project will also provide new marketing opportunities to the Feed the Future farmers of Northern Haiti. Positive results achieved recently through the FTFN project will be consolidated and scaled up. Activities will be implemented with a focus on sustainability and private sector engagement. FTFN interventions will also contribute to community and household resilience by improving access to irrigation water through pumps and irrigation canals. Additionally, hillside stabilization interventions will reduce the environmental impacts of flooding..

title.narrative: Pilot Project for Sustainable Electricity Distribution (PPSELD)

description.narrative: This contract will establish and operate the electric utility in Caracol, Haiti under the Pilot Project for Sustainable Electricity Distribution (PPSELD). For the past year, NRECA staff and volunteers have been focused on the CCEP to construct a distribution system to the town of Caracol and surrounding communities; PPSELD will build upon this success by operating the power plant from which CCEP derives its power and expanding the CCEP network to benefit additional communities close to Caracol. PPSELD is a three-year undertaking to establish a self-sustaining generation-distribution utility that will expand service from the CCEP customer base to include Limonade, Terrier Rouge, and Trou du Nord that are in close proximity to Caracol. In future years, PPSELD may expand service to additional communities if USAID and the Government of Haiti provide approval. The project is an incredible opportunity for both NRECA International and local counterparts to create a true example of a successful electric utility in Haiti.

title.narrative: Service Delivery Project (SSQH - Service de Santé de Qualité pour Haïti) - South

description.narrative: (Haiti): USAID's Health Service Delivery Project in the South (SSQH-South) provides access to, and increased utilization of, primary healthcare services at health facilities in six departments in south and central Haiti. Emphasis is placed on increasing the utilization of the MOH's integrated package of services at the primary care and community levels (particularly in rural or isolated areas). These services include pre- and post-natal care, family planning, nutrition, HIV/AIDS, TB, child health services including immunization and nutrition, sanitation and hygiene. With FY 2015 funds, the project will also provide staff training and site management support at the facility level, with an emphasis on enhancing the quality of its service delivery. The expected end result of the program is the improved health status of the Haitian population through better quality primary care and health referral networks, and more rigorous management practices at the facility and community levels.

(Haiti): The LEVE project will support small and medium enterprises that operate within industries assessed to have the best prospects for growth and job creation. Firms within the construction, apparel, and agribusiness value chains, including input suppliers and end-market buyers, as well as technical, business, and financial support services firms, will receive technical support. The project will help firms identify and take advantage of market opportunities, assist in developing product or service upgrading strategies, and train workers in accordance with identified skill requirements.Expected results include: greater integration of 2,000 micro, small, and medium enterprises in selected value chains; 14,000 people in new or better employment; twelve workforce development organizations more responsive to private sector demand.

Objectives for Haiti: USAID’s program will facilitate more productive and inclusive value chains, which will contribute to broad-based economic growth. The overarching goal of this project is to increase employment in Haiti.

(Haiti): .Evaluation and Survey Services (ESS) is a monitoring and evaluation platform contract used to design and carry out evaluation activities to support stronger results and to improve evidence-based programming. These efforts will facilitate informed program management decisions, shape the long-term strategic direction of Mission programs, and assess the results of ongoing activities. FY 2020 funds will be used to carry out various performance evaluations of several activities implemented within the economic growth, governance, agriculture, education and health sectors. Using FY2020 funding, ESS will continue with the impact evaluation of the Mission's early grade reading program started in FY 2017, conduct the midterm evaluations of the Project Supporting the Efficient Management of State Resources (GERE) and the Community Driven Development (CDD) project. ESS will also implement five (5) final performance evaluations among which the final evaluation of the RANFOSE, AKSYON, SANTE, JSSP and CEPPs Activities and two (2) baseline surveys: one for the Education Strong Beginning Activity and one for the DO2 Resilience Program currently under design. ESS will also start building monitoring and evaluation capacity among USAID, local research firms and consultants to enable them to use monitoring and evaluation data to support adaptive management in line with USAID policy, international standards, and best practices..

description.narrative: (Haiti): RAPIDE is a two-year activity aiming at ensuring better integration of children and youth who are blind and visually impaired into mainstream classrooms. USAID will assist the oldest Haitian NGO working for blind people in providing support with specialized teachers, adapted materials and after-school instruction. RAPIDE will also increase the availability of reading resources for children and youth with visual impairment. Specifically RAPIDE will set up a braille production unit that will produce books in braille, audio or relief, and provide access to specialized library services through braille reading clubs and computer rooms with communication technologies for the blind and visually impaired. Through this activity a greater number of children who are blind and visually impaired will have access to quality education services.

title.narrative: Support for the Electoral Process in Haiti - CEPPS IV (2015-2016)

description.narrative: (Haiti): Within the CEPPS consortium, The National Democratic Institute (NDI) helps to build the capacity of civil society organizations to provide credible oversight of the elections, mitigate the risk of electoral violence, and advocate for the compliance to the 30-percent gender quota. The International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES) builds the communications capacity of the electoral commission and works with it to ensure that women, persons with disabilities, and other marginalized communities are fully integrated in the electoral process. CEPPS is reinforcing the electoral authorities' capacity to conduct credible, inclusive, and legitimate elections that reflect the will of the Haitian people; strengthen the capacity of non-partisan election observers; and assist civil society organizations, political parties, and electoral authorities in increasing women's participation as voters, candidates, and poll-workers. A cost extension will allow CEPPS to conduct activities with newly elected officials; bolster transparency, communication between the population and the elected officials. It will also allow CEPPS to build on ongoing activities and be operational in-between elections leading up to the Senate elections to be held in 2016.

title.narrative: Evaluations of Food Security and Resilience Programming

description.narrative: IBTCI was contracted by USAID to conduct a final performance evaluation of the Haiti Multi-Year Assistance Programs (MYAPs) Program implemented through three implementing partners. These programs seek to reduce food insecurity and increased resiliency of vulnerable and extremely vulnerable rural households throughout Haiti. The evaluation will determine the overall impact of the program by investigating three major questions: (1) the extent to which the food security status of the targeted population has changed; (2) the extent to which the MYAPs programs have contributed to the resiliency of the targeted communities; and (3) the extent to which the various mothers clubs models implemented by the Title II cooperating sponsors are cost-effective. The evaluation is expected to help guide and optimize the effectiveness of future Food for Peace programming in Haiti, and compile the best practices and lessons learned.

description.narrative: USAIDs Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS) Project helps to provide continued support for the Haitian government for restoration, operation, and expansion of IFMS-related network infrastructure and the financial management systems. Activities include hardware and software procurement, implementation, and training across a broad spectrum of government financial functions. The project contributes to improvement of current IFMS functionality, access, security, and accountability; development of business continuity and contingency plans; and better alignment of the governments business processes and technology. Examples of progress include electronic submission of budget requests, improved monitoring and audit capabilities, increased management control of budget expenditures, greater transparency and accountability in revenue collection, and overall improved public services. Additionally, IFMS adequately serves end-users on the network from government ministries and independent oversight agencies, as well as regional entities, without performance degradation. The IFMS is intended to comprise software components in the governments public financial management function and support the ability to share data across ministries, resulting in greater financial efficiency, transparency, and accountability.

title.narrative: Ann ALE (Ann Aprann Li ak Ekri - Let's Learn to Read and Write)

description.narrative: (Haiti): USAID continues to assist the Government of Haiti (GOH) in improving children's reading and writing skills with evidence-based Haitian Creole and French instructional programs for grades one through four. Major activities include the development and implementation of reading and writing curricula, training and coaching teachers on appropriate instructional methods, provision of classroom libraries, assessment of student reading and writing abilities, and year-round reading programs to improve student retention and academic performance. Communication activities will increase public awareness of the importance of reading and writing. The expected results are strengthened government capacity to implement evidence-based approaches, improved learning outcomes, and the integration of this program into the national curriculum with the long-term objective of improved foundational skills to prepare Haitians for greater economic self-sufficiency.

description.narrative: The Electrical Substation Rehabilitation project aims to improve the physical infrastructure needed to reduce technical losses and enhance efficiencies of the EDH electrical distribution system. Based on assessments we conducted after the earthquake, we identified the repair and upgrade of these five substations to be critical priorities for the electrical sector. The underperformance of these substations is drastically reducing the systems capacity for transmission and distribution of electrical power.Activities. In November 2010, USAID signed a contract with AECOM to develop the technical specifications for the rehabilitation of the five substations located in the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area: Canape Vert, Carrefour Feuille, Toussaint Brave, Croix-des-Bouquets, and Nouveau Delmas. Through an open competition, we then awarded a contract for the rehabilitation of the substations to Perini Management Services, Inc. Rehabilitation activities have begun, and are scheduled for completion by November 2012.

title.narrative: Watershed Initiative for National Natural Environmental Resources (WINNER)

description.narrative: FtF West/ WINNER is a multi-sectoral program that aims to increase incomes in 2 U.S. Government development corridors Port-au-Prince, St. Marc. Through agricultural intensification, rehabilitation of rural infrastructure, support to post-harvest operations and good governance of natural resources, WINNER improves the livelihoods of targeted farmers. To reach these objectives, WINNER brings together farmers, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), agribusinesses, and government actors to comprehensively increase productivity and post-harvest efficiency, and improve the management and protection of the corridors key watersheds. WINNER uses a value chain approach for focus crops in the productive plains.

title.narrative: PROMARK: Strengthening and Expanding Social Marketing in Haiti

description.narrative: A significant percentage of Haitis population cannot afford health care and does not receive information on basic health issues. In response, USAID launched PROMARK to strengthen and expand social marketing of health-related products and services in Haiti and address gaps in behavior change communication and information campaigns. The PROMARK project is designed based on Ministry of Health (MOH) recommendations, both at the central and departmental levels. PROMARK promotes healthy behaviors related to reproductive health, family planning, maternal health, and child survival. A primary component of this strategy is the distribution of affordable condoms and other contraceptives, oral rehydration salts, and safe water products at commercial establishments, pharmacies, and private clinics throughout the country, thus making behavior change easier.

title.narrative: Sant pour le Dveloppement et la Stabilit d'Hati (SDSH) - Pwoj Djanm

description.narrative: The Sant pour le Dveloppement et la Stabilit dHati (SDSH) Projectknown as Pwoj Djanm (robust project) in Creoleand its all-Haitian team are working to increase availability of essential social services, reduce internal conflict, enable productive livelihoods that contribute to Haitis economic development, and build capacity as the foundation for progress. MSH and its partners will continue to support local service delivery NGOs by using performance-based contracts, a proven way to reinforce innovation and accountability; these NGOs will go on to become additional sources of technical assistance. Pwoj Djanm's focus is on supporting decentralization, strengthening public-sector capacity in service delivery, and supporting local NGO service delivery by leveraging funding from the commercial sector and other donors.

Port-au-Prince-Saint Marc Partnership represents a new and innovative approach to addressing the food security needs of the Haitian people. Haiti Port-au-Prince/Saint Marc Partnership will build on results achieved through Feed-the-Future/West (WINNER) to sustainable transform the agriculture sector; increase agricultural incomes; and contribute to improve the nutritional status of 60,000 beneficiary households in the Cul-de-Sac and Matheux corridors, as well as in mango production areas. This activity will be implemented over a three year period, partnering with a separate, five year Cooperative Agreement that will complement and reinforce the activities undertaken under this award. The Port-au-Prince/Saint-Marc Partnership also supports the USAID Forward Initiative and its goal of increasing the number of procurements directly with local organizations that will contribute to the achievement of objectives targeted by this award.

title.narrative: Reducing Vulnerabilities and Impacts of Neighborhood Emergencies (RAVINE)

description.narrative: The Reducing Vulnerabilities and Impacts of Neighborhood Emergencies (RAVINE) program, funded by USAID/OFDA, focuses on risk reduction activities in vulnerable urban ravine neighborhoods. Program interventions include reconstructing community-identified public infrastructure; training residents on safer, cost-effective building techniques; and increasing awareness of the impacts of solid waste.

UPGRADE (Urban Planning to Generate Resilience against Disaster Events) will focus on informal, densely-populated, impoverished urban areas in Ouanaminthe (Northeast) and Port-au-Prince (West). These neighborhoods have limited access to basic health, water and sanitation services. Many dwellings are made from substandard materials unable to withstand severe weather and seismic events. When disaster does strike, the lack of adequate roads, pedestrian pathways and community infrastructure inhibits evacuation and the delivery of humanitarian aid.

Improve the ability of the USG, host countries and other partners to prepare for and mitigate the effects of disasters, including both natural disasters and complex emergencies, taking into account the differences in men and womens freedom of movement and access to information. Activities under this component include any efforts to enhance the capacities of the USG (in Washington and in the field), humanitarian assistance providers, national host-country authorities, and local communities to engage in disaster reduction and response activities. Activities consist of standardized and coordinated assessments, monitoring, information sharing, data and situational analysis, joint planning; enhancement of coping mechanisms, including the capacity to address adaptation to constantly changing situations on the ground including climate variability and climate change.
